images.title: Sera in the Lamplit Court

Ordered dotted lines continue down neck and upper arms, spreading into dense constellations near wrists/hands; small normal non-glowing eyes. Sera is a practical learned craftsperson sitting sideways at a waist-high wooden bench in a stone courtyard sunk below street level. Three-quarter medium shot, hands and face clearly readable. Warm lamplight pools against cool blue evening from the opening high above. Two indistinct same-species neighbors cross a stone stair in the background, modest homes and real doors. Rich amber/teal, ordinary concentration, no heroic spell pose.

images.title: Hessa’s Winter Door
images.summary: Hessa repairs a bow at the threshold of a moorland household as rain sweeps over the marsh. The scene gives the Moor folk domestic life and an individual defender, without making their society merely a service to humans.
images.scene: Use ONLY take FOUR, BOTTOM LEFT, the lean adult Moor woman with high cheekbones, projecting narrow nose, tawny-grey facial fur and short continuous shoulder ruff. Preserve her nonhuman face and long hands/limbs. She sits at the doorway of her own modest timber-and-stone home above a rain-dark moor, carefully inspecting the curve of an unstrung longbow held across her lap. Natural broad fur locks frame a dark moss wool tunic, a simple belt and practical trousers; no flowers or druid crown. Her head turns toward the coming weather, calm and self-possessed. View from the warm interior looking obliquely out: one edge of a plain pot and hanging woven cloth inside, amber hearth bounce on face, cool silver rain and ochre reeds outside. A few other homes linked by short wooden walkways in middle distance, no vast fantasy village. The bow is a real tool with coherent grip and only TWO hands, not a weapon aimed at viewer. Quiet strong character, nature and household together, not idyllic storybook greenery.

images.title: A Camp before Rain
images.summary: Salt-variant Tavra and silt-variant Korr secure a caravan camp as a storm reaches the flats. Their shared anatomy stays visible across different colouring, while personal gear and an independent life suggest Fervor.
images.scene: Two RELATED variants of the SAME people. Main adult woman is TOP LEFT salt variant: warm ochre skin with softened pale stripes, swept low brow, sculpted cheeks, long arms and medium legs. Secondary man is BOTTOM LEFT silt variant: olive-brown skin and similar skull/body architecture, somewhat broader. No tails, no alien eyes. Tavra stands close at left three-quarter profile, turning toward the storm with one hand holding a tent guy rope taut; Korr farther back anchors the other rope to a wooden cart wheel, physically plausible work. A low caravan canvas awning rises between them, not huge pavilion. Practical individually repaired clothes: rust-red sleeveless quilted vest with obvious leather closures for Tavra, charcoal linen and patched brown wool for Korr; a sheathed short curved sword hangs securely at Tavra's hip, no costume ornament. White mineral flats and shallow brown runnels stretch toward bruised blue storm clouds; slanting late sun catches ochre faces and bleached ground. Rope and posture carry motion, two people cooperating as independent travelers; no marching army or uniform faction insignia. Warm mineral light against approaching rain, exciting ordinary-scale place.

images.title: Ilyra and the Unfinished Arch
images.summary: Ilyra sets a stone into an ordinary old arch using trained magic and a mason’s judgement. The scene tests how the proposed arm and body crests read with practical clothing and purposeful movement.
images.scene: Preserve this selected adult Crest folk woman exactly: swept fluted head crest, russet cheek marks, chalk-tan skin, slender strong proportions, small swept crests on shoulders/clavicles and outer upper arms/forearms, normal free joints and hands. Outfit fitted sleeveless indigo work tunic with linen underlayer, simple waist belt and one small stone mallet tucked through it; tailored openings let her anatomical crests show, never attach armor over them. She works in three-quarter view under an old masonry arch on a sunlit city terrace, one bare hand giving the final tiny adjustment to a heavy shaped stone levitating just above its timber support cradle. Her other hand rests on the support, clear contact and working balance; the stone is moving a few centimeters, not an exploding magic storm. Broad afternoon light rakes across real joints in the stone and her ridges. Distant high-fantasy rooftops suggested loosely beyond the arch, warm limestone against blue shade. images.title: Brann at the Low-Tide Road
images.summary: Brann steadies the gangplank of a grounded ferry while the last traveller crosses the tidal causeway. His broad body becomes a convincing ordinary presence, with protective choices suggesting Vigil rather than a compulsory faction uniform.
images.scene: Preserve the exact broad grey Coast folk man: deep rounded torso and belly, short sturdy legs, low neck, broad calm face, matte slate-blue hide and fine hands. NO TAIL. Ordinary adult height, not giant. He is Brann, a ferry keeper, in a short oiled-wool shoulder wrap with the original bone clasp, plain taupe trousers and sturdy practical foot wraps appropriate to his broad feet. Medium-wide side view on a rough stone tidal causeway at blue hour. He braces a thick wooden gangplank from a small physically grounded ferry with BOTH hands, letting a secondary cloaked adult traveler step safely off; his stance and the supported plank clearly make physical sense. The boat is tied with a real rope to a bollard. A plain warm lantern under its canopy, distant dark water advancing across sand, loose gull shapes and no spectacular sea creature. A worn small shield and short spear lie strapped inside the boat as ordinary protective kit, not held simultaneously. Cool turquoise dusk, warm lamp on his broad face and hands, weathered reality with a little hope.

images.summary: Brann becomes the human-scale anchor of a defensive spell as storm spray breaks around the crossing. The spell is a proposal for this character; it does not make the Coast folk natural ward-casters.
images.art: The same broad grey Coast folk ferryman Brann stands in three-quarter view on the RIGHT half of a storm-dark stone crossing, near the viewer. Preserve deep belly/torso, short sturdy legs, low neck, calm blunt face, fine hands, slate matte hide, NO TAIL and ordinary size. Short oiled-wool shoulder wrap with bone clasp, practical taupe trousers. A small battered wooden shield is planted on his left forearm with clear straps, angled outward; his right palm touches the stone post next to him.
